settings.heading: What does *your* pet need from a bed?
settings.text: Every bed we sell is sorted by the one thing that matters most — how your pet sleeps. Pick the colour that sounds like them.
settings.quiz_text: Answer four questions and we'll match them.

settings.title: They circle and circle before lying down
settings.text: Circling is how dogs build a nest. Endless circling usually means the bed isn't giving them the shape, or the sides, they're looking for.

settings.title: They're slower to get up in the morning
settings.text: Morning stiffness gets more common with age. A thin, flat bed lets hips and elbows press through to the hard floor — a deep, supportive one doesn't.

settings.title: You can feel the floor through the middle
settings.text: Press your hand into the spot where they lie. If it sinks straight through, the filling has flattened and it's no longer doing its job.

settings.title: They pick the sofa, the rug — anywhere else
settings.text: Pets vote with their paws. If they stretch out everywhere but their bed, it's usually too small, too enclosed or too soft to stretch out on.

settings.title: They squeeze into boxes, baskets and laundry piles
settings.text: Burrowers and cats want to feel held. A flat, open bed leaves them hunting for somewhere that wraps around them.

settings.heading: Five signs their bed has *stopped working.*
settings.text: Pets never complain about a bad bed. They just quietly stop using it — or keep using it, and feel it in the morning.
settings.cta_intro: Recognise one? Find the fix in 60 seconds.

settings.title: Somewhere to rest their head

settings.title: Warmth that wraps around them

settings.title: Easy to keep fresh

settings.question: How do I choose the right size?
settings.answer: Measure your pet from nose to base of tail while they're stretched out asleep, then add 15–20cm — that's the length of bed to look for. Curlers can go a little smaller; sprawlers should go bigger. Not sure? The Sleep Match gives you a size in 60 seconds, and our size guide goes breed by breed.

settings.question: Which bed is best for an older dog?
settings.answer: Start with our Support beds: memory or orthopaedic foam that spreads their weight evenly, ideally with a low front so they can step straight in. A bed isn't a treatment — if your dog is stiff or sore, keep talking to your vet — but a supportive surface makes the many hours they spend lying down far more comfortable.

settings.question: My dog gets anxious. Can a bed help?
settings.answer: Many nervous dogs settle more easily in a Calm bed. Raised, bolstered sides give them something to lean into and a wall at their back — the way they'd curl up against a littermate. It isn't a cure for anxiety, but it gives them a safe spot that's always theirs.
